items.title: `123456' password used in Danish CPR data breach
items.summary: At least three accounts at the Danish IT company Pays, including an administrator account, used the password "123456" when a hacker gained access to Denmark's central civil registration system, exposing data linked to around 8.8 million CPR numbers. The hacker reportedly got in using a leaked password from a former employee and had access to the register for 21 days and 17 hours, starting September 10, and told Politiken there were no plans to sell or publish the data.

items.title: Talorys – A self-hosted personal AI agent on Cloudflare's free tier
items.summary: Talorys is an open-source personal AI agent that runs in your own Cloudflare account, offering chat, memory, tasks, notes, and scheduled reminders. It deploys with a single command (npx create-talorys@latest), is designed for Cloudflare's free tier, is single-user, and ships with no telemetry.

items.title: Apple/macOS silently removed from official Unix registry
items.summary: The Open Group's official register of UNIX certified products no longer lists Apple or macOS, leaving IBM's AIX and z/OS and Hewlett Packard Enterprise's HP-UX among the remaining certified systems. UNIX certification is the vendor-neutral benchmark that qualifies an operating system to use the UNIX trademark under the Single UNIX Specification.
